answer: The vertex decay curve is applied at each close, karst records the drop, and island recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 5 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. A farm that parks aliases between attacks thus finds them worthless when it returns to them. That bill is paid per identity, so 281 aliases cost 35 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
